log.why: Testing ompF directly targets the highest-posterior gene (0.411) and can boost it near 0.89 in one plate.
Testing 1 uM on Ticket 2 splits the dose threshold posterior 0.394 vs 0.606 while Ticket 1's plate incubates.
Ticket 1 has less time left and lacZ leads at 0.538; E1 strongly confirms lacZ if positive or rules it out.
Ticket 2 has less time than Ticket 3, and 3 uM splits its posterior nearly in half (0.471 vs 0.529).
E4 splits Ticket 2 cleanly at 10 uM (0.611 vs 0.389) and starts incubation immediately to overlap with publishing Ticket 1.
Ticket 3 has 0.461 posterior mass at or below 10 uM, so E4 splits the hypothesis space nearly evenly while Ticket 2 incubates.
Ticket 2 has 41 s left and E3 tests the main 3 uM rival against 10 uM while allowing parallel Ticket 1 publishing.
Ticket 1 has only 23 s left and lacZ already holds 0.929 posterior probability.
Ticket 2 expires in 18s with 3 and 10 uM close (0.505 vs 0.379); E3 cleanly separates them before publishing.
Ticket 2 has 10 s left, so E3 cannot finish before publishing; claiming 3 uM at 0.505 posterior avoids a -30 expiration penalty.
Ticket 3 expires in 19 s; E3 splits the posterior nearly evenly at 3 µM (0.477 vs 0.523) before publishing.
Ticket 4 expires in 27s; E9 splits prior mass 0.566 vs 0.434, raising the top gene posterior above 0.50 in one plate.
Ticket 4 expires in 9s with araC at 0.507 posterior, giving positive expected value versus -30 expiration penalty.
Testing rpoB on Ticket 5 directly targets the 0.393 leading hypothesis; a positive result yields 0.879 posterior for a fast publish.
With 22 s left and incubators free, testing dnaK (highest posterior 0.318) on Ticket 7 can raise confidence to 0.840 in one plate.
With 3 seconds left, publish Ticket 5 because rpoB has a high 0.879 posterior after E0 showed phenotype loss.
